clue.text: Almost entirely at sea?

definitions.meaning: for the most part, generally, mostly
out on the ocean, the main being an old word for the open sea

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second, literal reading: the main is a poetic name for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means mostly, and read literally it places something out on the ocean.

clue.text: I attack religion

parts.note: to slam is to criticise or attack harshly

explanation.surface: Someone declares they will go after a faith.
explanation.definitionFit: The faith of Muslims is a major world religion.

clue.text: Steak done differently in French town

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit inside the name of the town

parts.note: Tours is a city on the Loire in France

indicators.note: done differently means the letters of done are arranged another way

explanation.surface: A steak is cooked in some other style in a French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges the four letters of 'done', and 'in' puts the result inside the French city on the Loire.
explanation.definitionFit: A tournedos is a small round cut of beef fillet, a kind of steak.

clue.text: Purgative stops meals being digested

indicators.note: food being digested is broken down, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A laxative halts meals as they pass through the gut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being digested' tells you to rearrange the ten letters of STOPS MEALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom salts, magnesium sulphate, are taken as a laxative, a classic purgative.

clue.text: Forgive sailor's answer

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is a sailor
to solve is to find the answer to

explanation.surface: Pardon the reply a seaman gives.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has' and is a link: the sailor has the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To absolve someone is to release them from guilt, to pardon them.

clue.text: Sentinel half-heartedly disturbed composer

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown into disorder, so they are rearranged
the heart of the word is its middle pair of letters, and half of that pair is removed

explanation.surface: A guard on duty, only lukewarm about it, troubled a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: SENTINEL's heart is TI; 'half-heartedly' drops the T, leaving SENINEL, which 'disturbed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Carl Nielsen was a Danish composer of symphonies and concertos.

clue.text: Pottery expert drinks port

indicators.note: something that drinks takes liquid in, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: deft means skilful or expert
port is the left side of a ship, and L stands for left

explanation.surface: A connoisseur downs a glass of fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the wine but is the left side of a ship, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Delftware is tin-glazed pottery named after the Dutch city where it was made.

clue.text: Knife gives Penny trouble

parts.note: d was the symbol for an old British penny, from the Latin denarius
to irk is to annoy or trouble

explanation.surface: A blade brings difficulty to a woman called Penny.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirk is a short dagger, especially the Scottish Highland kind.

clue.text: Sunday spent in Cornish resort rambling

indicators.note: time spent in a place is passed inside it, so this letter goes inside the resort

parts.note: Looe is a seaside town in Cornwall, south-west England

explanation.surface: A weekend day passed at a seaside town in Cornwall, wandering about.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose and rambling both describe talk or writing that lacks tight structure.

clue.text: Whizz round whirlpool on soft toy

indicators.note: one piece goes round the others, enclosing them

parts.note: to tear is to rush or whizz along
an eddy is a small whirlpool
B marks a soft pencil lead, as H marks a hard one

explanation.surface: Someone speeds about a swirling current riding a cuddly plaything.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the whirlpool above the soft letter, and 'round' wraps the whizz word around both. 'soft' comes from pencil grades, not the usual piano P.
explanation.definitionFit: A teddy bear is the classic stuffed plush plaything for children.

clue.text: US oil liquidated in French money

indicators.note: something liquidated is broken up or wound down, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: American petroleum assets are sold off for euros in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquidated' rearranges US OIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The louis, or louis d'or, was an old French gold coin.

clue.text: Damage in a weapon is an obscenity

indicators.note: the damage word goes inside the weapon word

parts.note: a sword is a bladed weapon
wear is damage from use, as in wear and tear

explanation.surface: Harm done inside a weapon counts as something indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: A swear word is a profane or offensive term, an obscenity.

clue.text: Note a register of some painters

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, a half note
a list or register is a written record of names

explanation.surface: Jot down a roll of certain artists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' is the musical note MINIM, not a jotting.
explanation.definitionFit: Minimalist describes artists such as Donald Judd whose work uses the barest forms, so it belongs to some painters.

clue.text: Turkish officer seizes five of a group of girls

indicators.note: a piece that seizes another holds it inside

parts.note: a bey was a governor or officer in the Ottoman Empire
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: An Ottoman official grabs five young women from a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Bevy is a collective noun for a company of women or girls.

clue.text: British offices show approval for witchcraft!

parts.note: offices are rooms where work is done
to tick something off on a list shows it is approved

explanation.surface: Bureaucrats in Britain approve of sorcery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'witchcraft!' is read as a witch's craft, the vehicle she flies, not her magic.
explanation.definitionFit: A broomstick is the flying vessel of a witch in folklore, hence a witch craft.

clue.text: Ted adopts new plan at this stage in the match

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: Ted and Ed are both short forms of Edward
a game is a scheme or plan, as in what is his game?

explanation.surface: Ted takes up a fresh strategy at this point in the contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted becomes the other short form of Edward, ED, which takes in N.
explanation.definitionFit: The endgame is the final phase of a chess game or similar contest.

clue.text: Wrinkles between features in a premature state

indicators.note: the wrinkles go between the two parts of the other word

parts.note: ears are features of the head
lines are wrinkles on the skin

explanation.surface: Creases between facial parts suggest someone aged before their time.
explanation.definitionFit: Earliness is the condition of being early, coming before the due time.

clue.text: Run true to form in school

indicators.note: the letters are put together to form a new word, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A runner performs as expected at school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'true to form' looks like an idiom, but 'to form' rearranges RUN TRUE.
explanation.definitionFit: To school and to nurture both mean to train or bring up.

clue.text: Clothing subject to deterioration

parts.note: under means subject to, as in under orders
wear is gradual deterioration from use

explanation.surface: Garments liable to wear out.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear is clothing worn beneath outer garments.

clue.text: Award of firm that's invested in mechanical procedure

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so this piece goes inside the other

parts.note: rote is mechanical repetition, as in learning by rote
set means firm or solid, as jelly sets

explanation.surface: A prize for a company that has put money into automated routines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'firm' looks like a company, but it is the adjective SET.
explanation.definitionFit: A rosette is a ribbon badge given as a prize, at shows for example.

clue.text: Greeting bishop during farewell parade

indicators.note: one piece comes during, so inside, the other

parts.note: an exit is a departure, a leave-taking
hi is a greeting
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman waves hello in the middle of a leaving procession.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhibit something is to display or parade it publicly.

clue.text: Coloured tuber rejected as the buyer wishes

indicators.note: something rejected is turned back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: red is a colour
a root vegetable, such as a beet, is a tuber in loose usage

explanation.surface: A customer sends back a dyed potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns REDROOT back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: Made to order means made to the customer's specification.

clue.text: Paint a casual worker over time

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits over, above, the next

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Decorate as a part-timer for an age.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a paint made with egg yolk as the binder.

clue.text: Fancy model endlessly

indicators.note: without its end, the final letter is dropped

parts.note: an ideal is a model to aim for

explanation.surface: An expensive fashion model who never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of IDEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a notion or idea, as in a passing fancy.

clue.text: Particularly old painting put up

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means written upwards, so read backwards

parts.note: painting is art

explanation.surface: A notably antique picture gets hung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reads like hanging a picture, but it reverses ART in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra used adverbially means especially, as in extra careful.

clue.text: Asks for lift from sailors? That could be unpleasant!

parts.note: a hitchhiker thumbs a lift
a crew is the company of sailors on a ship

explanation.surface: Hitchhiking with seamen could turn nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a jokey understatement for an instrument of torture.
explanation.definitionFit: A thumbscrew is a torture device, so its use would certainly be unpleasant.

clue.text: Attached to the top of your willow tree

parts.note: with means attached to or accompanying

indicators.note: in a down light the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Fastened to the crown of your willow.
explanation.definitionFit: A withy is a willow, especially one with flexible shoots for basketry.

clue.text: Give out over a period

indicators.note: turned over, the word is reversed

parts.note: a period is a length of time

explanation.surface: Hand things out across a span of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns TIME back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out or discharge, as light or sound.

clue.text: Worthy of respect, 'e 'as firm protecting 'im

parts.note: the dropped-aitch he gives E

indicators.note: one piece shelters the other by enclosing it

parts.note: stable means firm or steady
the dropped-aitch him gives IM

explanation.surface: A Cockney says he is a solid sort who looks after his mate.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped aitches mimic Cockney speech; 'as (has) is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Estimable means deserving esteem, admirable.

clue.text: Foolish writer retired in Italy

indicators.note: the reversed writer goes inside the country code

parts.note: IT is the international vehicle code for Italy

indicators.note: retiring is withdrawing, going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A silly author retires to Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns the writing tool back to front before 'in' sets it inside the country code.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy or lacking sense, hence foolish.

clue.text: Father makes Bob sarcastic

parts.note: bob was slang for a shilling, abbreviated s in old British money
a tart remark is sharp or sarcastic

explanation.surface: Dad turns a man called Bob caustic.
explanation.walkthrough: A bob was an old British shilling, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: To father a scheme is to originate or begin it.

clue.text: Computer hobbyist found in loch is a writer

indicators.note: this piece is found inside the other

parts.note: Loch Tay is a lake in the Scottish Highlands
a hacker is a computer enthusiast

explanation.surface: A coding enthusiast discovered in a Scottish lake turns out to be an author.
explanation.definitionFit: William Makepeace Thackeray was the Victorian novelist of Vanity Fair.
